cards.back: Staged, unstaged and untracked changes, plus the current branch.

cards.front: How do you stage only part of a file?
cards.why: Lets one file's changes go into separate commits.
Fetch first when you want to look before changing your branch.

cards.front: How do you see what a commit changed?
Create a branch and switch to it in one step?

cards.back: Seeing how branches split and merged, one line per commit.

cards.front: Unstage a file but keep its changes?
Throw away uncommitted changes in one file?
cards.why: There's no undo for this; the changes were never saved in git.

cards.front: Fix the message of the last commit (not pushed yet)?

cards.back: `git revert <commit>` adds a new commit that reverses it.
cards.why: Rewriting pushed history breaks other people's clones.

cards.front: Find a commit you lost after a reset?
cards.back: `git reflog` lists where HEAD has been.
Memory of new facts drops fast at first, then more slowly.
cards.why: Each review flattens the curve, so gaps can grow.

cards.front: Why test yourself instead of re-reading?
cards.back: Recalling an answer strengthens memory far more than seeing it again.
cards.why: Called the testing effect or retrieval practice.

cards.back: One fact or one decision, with a short answer.
cards.why: Small cards are graded honestly; big ones get half-known.

cards.front: What should you do with a card you keep missing?
cards.back: Split it or add a `why` that gives it meaning.

cards.front: Why mix topics in one session?
cards.back: Interleaving makes you pick the right idea, not just repeat one.
